<think>
The problem asks me to check if all elements in a list share the same type using the `?` operator.
In Falcon, the `?` operator can test for types: `v ? number`, `v ? text`, `v ? list`, `v ? dict`.
My plan: get the type of the first element, then iterate over all elements and check each one matches.
To "get" the type I'll use a helper that returns a string label: try `? number`, then `? text`, then `? list`, then `? dict`.
Then for `isHomogeneous`, get type of first element, iterate using `for (item in lst)` and check `item ? <that type>`.
If all match, return `true`, else `false`.
Note: Falcon uses `listLen()` for list length and `add()` for list append, and logical operators are `&&` and `!`.
</think>
```falcon
func typeOf(v) = {
  if (v ? number) {
    "number"
  } else if (v ? text) {
    "text"
  } else if (v ? list) {
    "list"
  } else {
    "dict"
  }
}

func isHomogeneous(lst) = {
  if (lst.listLen() == 0) {
    true
  } else {
    local t = typeOf(lst[1])
    local ok = true
    for (item in lst) {
      if (typeOf(item) !== t) {
        ok = false
      }
    }
    ok
  }
}

println(isHomogeneous([1, "hello", 3]))
println(isHomogeneous(["a", "b", "c"]))
```

Write `titleCase(s)` — capitalise the first letter of each word (split at spaces, uppercase first char, rejoin with `_`). Test `"hello world from falcon"`.

uppercase it, then append the rest of the word: `word.segment(2, word.textLen() - 1)`.

```falcon
func capitalizeWord(w) = {
  if (w.textLen() == 0) {
    ""
  } else {
    w.segment(1, 1).uppercase() _ w.segment(2, w.textLen() - 1)
  }
}

func titleCase(s) = {
  local words = s.splitAtSpaces()
```

Write `slugify(s)` — lowercases `s` and replaces spaces with `"-"`. Test `"Hello World Example"` → `"hello-world-example"`.

<think>

First call `.lowercase()` to get the lowercase version.
Then iterate character by character: if char is " ", replace with "-", else keep.

```falcon
func slugify(s) = {
  local lower = s.lowercase()
  local result = ""
  for (i: 1 .. lower.textLen()) {
    local ch = lower.segment(i, 1)

      result = result _ "-"
```

Write `interleave(s1, s2)` — interleave characters of two strings using `segment(i, 1)` in a loop. Test `("abc", "123")` → `"a1b2c3"`.

<think>
interleave(s1, s2): interleave characters from two strings alternately.
Take character from s1 at position 1, then from s2 at position 1, then s1 position 2, etc.
Continue until one string is exhausted, then append the remaining characters of the longer string.
In Falcon: `s.segment(i, 1)` gives character at position i (start, length).
`textLen()` gives string length.
Loop from 1 to max(s1.textLen(), s2.textLen()), conditionally picking from each.
</think>
```falcon
func interleave(s1, s2) = {
  local result = ""
  local len1 = s1.textLen()
  local len2 = s2.textLen()
  local maxLen = if (len1 > len2) { len1 } else { len2 }
  for (i: 1 .. maxLen) {
    if (i <= len1) {
      result = result _ s1.segment(i, 1)
    }
    if (i <= len2) {
      result = result _ s2.segment(i, 1)
    }
  }
  result
}

```
